Reframed with insights from the Financial Stability Report (FSR): The statement’s candid acknowledgment of severe pandemic-driven hardship and elevated uncertainty is consistent with the FSR’s assessment that COVID-19 weighed heavily on the U.S. economy and financial system. The FSR highlights still-elevated vulnerabilities—high business leverage and default risk, ongoing stress on small and medium-sized businesses and some households, weakness in commercial real estate, fragilities among nonbank mortgage servicers, and the potential for renewed funding-market strains if risk appetite falls. Offsetting these risks, overall financial conditions are accommodative, supported by the zero to 0.25 percent policy rate, continued purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, and an array of liquidity and credit backstops (CPFF, SMCCF, TALF, MLF), along with expanded dollar swap lines and the FIMA repo facility. These measures sustained market functioning and credit availability and helped anchor inflation expectations alongside the shift to average-inflation targeting and explicit forward guidance. Net tone: cautious due to persistent pandemic and medium-term risks, but materially buffered by credible policy support and improved market functioning relative to the spring.
